paras.text: Meaning of the value of money
paras.urdu: زر کی قدر کا مفہوم Meaning

paras.text: By the value of money is meant that power of it by virtue of which it can obtain other things in its exchange. In other words its meaning is the exchange power, i.e. purchasing power, of money, e.g. if for one hundred rupees ten kilos of flour are obtained, then the value of one hundred rupees is equal to ten kilos of flour. In contrast, if for one hundred rupees eight kilos of flour are obtained, its meaning will be that the value of money has become less than before. In contrast, if in one hundred rupees twelve kilos of flour are obtained, its meaning will be that the value of money has increased from before. As it were, an inverse relation is found between the value of money and the prices of things. If prices rise, the value of money will become less; and if prices fall, the value of money increases.

sections.theory:
Thus we can also say that by dividing the gross national product by the quantity of money, the velocity of circulation of money is obtained.

Value of Money

Meaning of the value of money

By the value of money is meant that power of it by virtue of which it can obtain other things in its exchange. In other words its meaning is the exchange power, i.e. purchasing power, of money, e.g. if for one hundred rupees ten kilos of flour are obtained, then the value of one hundred rupees is equal to ten kilos of flour. In contrast, if for one hundred rupees eight kilos of flour are obtained, its meaning will be that the value of money has become less than before. In contrast, if in one hundred rupees twelve kilos of flour are obtained, its meaning will be that the value of money has increased from before. As it were, an inverse relation is found between the value of money and the prices of things. If prices rise, the value of money will become less; and if prices fall, the value of money increases.

Quantity Theory of Money

Introduction

This theory was presented by the American economist Professor Irving Fisher. In this theory Fisher gave a famous equation, with the help of which the relation of prices with the quantity of money and the circulation of money has been described. It is stated thus:

Definition

“If the quantity of money is doubled, the prices of goods become double and the value of money remains half. In contrast, if the quantity of money is made half, the prices of goods become half and the value of money becomes double, provided other conditions remain as they are.”

An economist has stated its definition thus.

“The Quantity Theory of Money States That movements in the price level are determined largely by movement in the nominal quantity of money” (F&D)

In short, the price level generally depends on the quantity of money. An economist explains this theory thus. Suppose that the government suddenly prints some more notes and distributes one hundred rupees to every citizen. Having got this gift, people will go out into the markets to buy the goods of their need. But since no increase has taken place in the stock or supply of things, the price of things will rise. From this it becomes known that an increase in the quantity of money becomes the cause of an increase in prices and a decrease in the value of money.

Professor Irving Fisher has presented the quantity theory of money in the following equation, which is called the transaction equation (Transaction Equation).

$P = \dfrac{MV + M'V'}{T}$

P = Price level

sections.content:
Thus we can also say that by dividing the gross national product by the quantity of money, the velocity of circulation of money is obtained.

Value of Money

Meaning of the value of money

By the value of money is meant that power of it by virtue of which it can obtain other things in its exchange. In other words its meaning is the exchange power, i.e. purchasing power, of money, e.g. if for one hundred rupees ten kilos of flour are obtained, then the value of one hundred rupees is equal to ten kilos of flour. In contrast, if for one hundred rupees eight kilos of flour are obtained, its meaning will be that the value of money has become less than before. In contrast, if in one hundred rupees twelve kilos of flour are obtained, its meaning will be that the value of money has increased from before. As it were, an inverse relation is found between the value of money and the prices of things. If prices rise, the value of money will become less; and if prices fall, the value of money increases.

Quantity Theory of Money

Introduction

This theory was presented by the American economist Professor Irving Fisher. In this theory Fisher gave a famous equation, with the help of which the relation of prices with the quantity of money and the circulation of money has been described. It is stated thus:

Definition

“If the quantity of money is doubled, the prices of goods become double and the value of money remains half. In contrast, if the quantity of money is made half, the prices of goods become half and the value of money becomes double, provided other conditions remain as they are.”

An economist has stated its definition thus.

“The Quantity Theory of Money States That movements in the price level are determined largely by movement in the nominal quantity of money” (F&D)

In short, the price level generally depends on the quantity of money. An economist explains this theory thus. Suppose that the government suddenly prints some more notes and distributes one hundred rupees to every citizen. Having got this gift, people will go out into the markets to buy the goods of their need. But since no increase has taken place in the stock or supply of things, the price of things will rise. From this it becomes known that an increase in the quantity of money becomes the cause of an increase in prices and a decrease in the value of money.

Professor Irving Fisher has presented the quantity theory of money in the following equation, which is called the transaction equation (Transaction Equation).

$P = \dfrac{MV + M'V'}{T}$

P = Price level

paras.text: This equation can also be written thus.
paras.urdu: اس مساوات کو ایسے بھی لکھ سکتے ہیں۔

paras.text: Price multiplied by trade means the total value of all goods and services, whose meaning is how much money is required to buy all goods and services. As it were, the left-hand element of the equation shows the “demand for money”. On the other side, if the quantity of money is multiplied by its velocity of circulation, and credit money is multiplied by its own velocity of circulation, then from the sum of both (MV + M′V′) the total quantity of money will be found. As it were, the right-hand element of the equation shows the “supply of money”. And thus the above equation is the equation of the demand for and supply of money, i.e. the demand for money and the supply of money are equal to each other.
paras.urdu: قیمت ضرب تجارت سے مراد ہے۔ تمام اشیاء و خدمات کی مجموعی مالیت جس کا مطلب یہ ہے کہ تمام اشیاء و خدمات کو خریدنے کے لیے کتنی رقم درکار ہے۔ گویا مساوات کے بائیں طرف کا رکن ”زر کی طلب“ کو ظاہر کرتا ہے دوسری طرف زر کی مقدار کو اس کی گردش کی رفتار سے ضرب دی جائے اور اعتباری زر کو اس کی اپنی رفتار گردش ضرب دی جائے تو دونوں کے مجموعہ سے (MV + M′V′) زر کی کل مقدار کو معلوم کر لیا جائے گا۔ گویا مساوات کے دائیں طرف کا رکن ”زر کی رسد“ کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ اور یوں مذکورہ بالا مساوات زر کی طلب اور زر کی رسد کی مساوات ہے یعنی زر کی طلب اور زر کی رسد ایک دوسرے کے برابر ہے۔

sections.theory:
M = Quantity of Money

V = Velocity of Money

M' = Credit Money

V' = Velocity of Credit Money

T = Transaction Performed by money.

This equation can also be written thus.

$PT = MV + M'V'$

Price multiplied by trade means the total value of all goods and services, whose meaning is how much money is required to buy all goods and services. As it were, the left-hand element of the equation shows the “demand for money”. On the other side, if the quantity of money is multiplied by its velocity of circulation, and credit money is multiplied by its own velocity of circulation, then from the sum of both (MV + M′V′) the total quantity of money will be found. As it were, the right-hand element of the equation shows the “supply of money”. And thus the above equation is the equation of the demand for and supply of money, i.e. the demand for money and the supply of money are equal to each other.

To present the above equation in an easy form, by eliminating M′ (i.e. the quantity of credit money) and V′ (i.e. the circulation of credit money) it can also be written thus.

$P = \dfrac{MV}{T}$

Suppose that:

$\text{Quantity of money } (M) = 100, \quad \text{velocity of circulation } (V) = 5, \quad \text{quantity of goods } (T) = 250$

Then:

$P = \dfrac{100 \times 5}{250} \qquad P = \text{Rs } 2$

If:

$M = 200,\; V = 5,\; T = 250 \qquad P = \dfrac{200 \times 5}{250} \qquad P = \text{Rs } 4$

In this equation, by doubling the quantity of money (M), its price too has become double, whereas in it the value of money remains half.

اس مساوات کو ایسے بھی لکھ سکتے ہیں۔

$PT = MV + M'V'$

قیمت ضرب تجارت سے مراد ہے۔ تمام اشیاء و خدمات کی مجموعی مالیت جس کا مطلب یہ ہے کہ تمام اشیاء و خدمات کو خریدنے کے لیے کتنی رقم درکار ہے۔ گویا مساوات کے بائیں طرف کا رکن ”زر کی طلب“ کو ظاہر کرتا ہے دوسری طرف زر کی مقدار کو اس کی گردش کی رفتار سے ضرب دی جائے اور اعتباری زر کو اس کی اپنی رفتار گردش ضرب دی جائے تو دونوں کے مجموعہ سے (MV + M′V′) زر کی کل مقدار کو معلوم کر لیا جائے گا۔ گویا مساوات کے دائیں طرف کا رکن ”زر کی رسد“ کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ اور یوں مذکورہ بالا مساوات زر کی طلب اور زر کی رسد کی مساوات ہے یعنی زر کی طلب اور زر کی رسد ایک دوسرے کے برابر ہے۔

مذکورہ مساوات کو آسان شکل میں پیش کرنے کیلئے M′ (یعنی اعتباری زر کی مقدار) اور V′ (یعنی اعتباری زر کی گردش) کو ختم کر کے یوں بھی لکھا جا سکتا ہے۔

$P = \dfrac{MV}{T}$

فرض کیا کہ:

$\text{Quantity of money } (M) = 100, \quad \text{velocity of circulation } (V) = 5, \quad \text{quantity of goods } (T) = 250$

ہو تو:

$P = \dfrac{100 \times 5}{250} \qquad P = \text{Rs } 2$

اگر:

$M = 200,\; V = 5,\; T = 250 \qquad P = \dfrac{200 \times 5}{250} \qquad P = \text{Rs } 4$

اس مساوات میں زر کی مقدار (M) کو دو گنا کرنے سے اس کی قیمت بھی دگنی ہو گئی ہے جبکہ اس میں زر کی قدر نصف رہ جاتی ہے۔

$P = \dfrac{100 \times 5}{250} \qquad P = \text{Rs } 2$

که:

$M = 200,\; V = 5,\; T = 250 \qquad P = \dfrac{200 \times 5}{250} \qquad P = \text{Rs } 4$

په دې معادله کې د پیسو د مقدار (M) په دوه چنده کولو بیه یې هم دوه چنده شوې، حال دا چې د پیسو ارزښت پکې نیمایي پاتې کېږي.
